title: Rigveda 10.127: Hymn to Night (Ratri Sukta)
source: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 48 (1711 CE (colophon: Saṃvat 1768)), OPenn, Public Domain Mark + Aufrecht's accented text (GRETIL) + Griffith's English (VedaWeb)
description: Rigveda 10.127: Hymn to Night (Ratri Sukta): Sanskrit text and Griffith's English, each verse linked to the page of a 1711 Rigveda manuscript (Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 48) that carries it.
introduction:
Rigveda 10.127 is a hymn of 8 verses addressed to the night. It stands in book (maṇḍala) 10, the last and latest book. The Rigveda is the oldest collection of Sanskrit hymns, composed in the second half of the second millennium BCE and handed down orally for many centuries before it was written down.

The manuscript shown is Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 48 (University of Pennsylvania), a paper manuscript of the eighth aṣṭaka (RV 10.46-10.191) of the Ṛgveda Saṃhitā in Devanāgarī, 158 leaves, 6 lines to the page, with the accents marked in red; the scribe's colophon on fol. 158 gives Saṃvat 1768 (1711 CE); this hymn stands on fol. 113v-114v. Each section below gives the verses that end on one page; the page boundaries were read on the images (the opening words of every page), not counted out. Like most Rigveda manuscripts, Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 48 writes a repeated refrain in short form after its first occurrence (for example kasmai° for kasmai devāya haviṣā vidhema); the Sanskrit shown is the full text of Aufrecht's edition.
translator_notes: Sanskrit: Aufrecht's edition (1877) with the Vedic accents, as entered by van Nooten and Holland (GRETIL).

English: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Rigveda (1889-1892; 2nd ed. 1896-1897), from the VedaWeb digital text; OCR slips in that text were corrected against the printed 2nd edition (data/sources/rigveda/griffith_errata.json).
This manuscript inserts khila verses (supplementary hymns outside Aufrecht's text) at some hymn ends; they are noted in the section notes and not reproduced.

translation.original_ref: RV 10.127.1-7 (aṣṭaka 8, adhyāya 7, varga 14); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 48 fol. 114r
translation.original_text:
1rātrī̱ vy a̍khyad āya̱tī pu̍ru̱trā de̱vy a1̱̍kṣabhi̍ḥ | viśvā̱ adhi̱ śriyo̍ 'dhita ||
2orv a̍prā̱ ama̍rtyā ni̱vato̍ de̱vy u1̱̍dvata̍ḥ | jyoti̍ṣā bādhate̱ tama̍ḥ ||
3nir u̱ svasā̍ram askṛto̱ṣasa̍ṁ de̱vy ā̍ya̱tī | aped u̍ hāsate̱ tama̍ḥ ||
4sā no̍ a̱dya yasyā̍ va̱yaṁ ni te̱ yāma̱nn avi̍kṣmahi | vṛ̱kṣe na va̍sa̱tiṁ vaya̍ḥ ||
5ni grāmā̍so avikṣata̱ ni pa̱dvanto̱ ni pa̱kṣiṇa̍ḥ | ni śye̱nāsa̍ś cid a̱rthina̍ḥ ||
6yā̱vayā̍ vṛ̱kya1̱̍ṁ vṛka̍ṁ ya̱vaya̍ ste̱nam ū̍rmye | athā̍ naḥ su̱tarā̍ bhava ||
7upa̍ mā̱ pepi̍śa̱t tama̍ḥ kṛ̱ṣṇaṁ vya̍ktam asthita | uṣa̍ ṛ̱ṇeva̍ yātaya ||
translation.text:
1WITH all her eyes the Goddess Night looks forth approaching many a spot: She hath put all her glories on.
2Immortal. she hath filled the waste, the Goddess hath filled height and depth: She conquers darkness with her light.
3The Goddess as she comes hath set the Dawn her Sister in her place: And then the darkness vanishes.
4So favour us this night, O thou whose pathways we have visited As birds their nest upon the tree.
5The villagers have sought their homes, and all that walks and all that flies, Even the falcons fain for prey.
6Keep off the she-wolf and the wolf, O Urmya, keep the thief away; Easy be thou for us to pass.
7Clearly hath she come nigh to me who decks the dark with richest hues: O Morning, cancel it like debts.
translation.scan_note: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 48, fol. 114r (OPenn image 113, lower leaf). Checked on the image: the Rigveda text on this page begins in RV 10.127.1 ‹viśvā adhi śriyo 'dhita›. The next page with Rigveda text, fol. 114v, begins in RV 10.127.8 ‹rātri stomaṁ na jigyuṣe›. Verses 10.127.1-7 end on this page; 10.127.1 begins on fol. 113v.

translation.original_ref: RV 10.127.8 (aṣṭaka 8, adhyāya 7, varga 14); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 48 fol. 114v
translation.original_text: <sup>8</sup>upa̍ te̱ gā i̱vāka̍raṁ vṛṇī̱ṣva du̍hitar divaḥ | rātri̱ stoma̱ṁ na ji̱gyuṣe̍ ||
translation.text: <sup>8</sup>These have I brought to thee like kine. O Night, thou Child of Heaven, accept This laud as for a conqueror.
translation.scan_note: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 48, fol. 114v (OPenn image 114, upper leaf). Checked on the image: the Rigveda text on this page begins in RV 10.127.8 ‹rātri stomaṁ na jigyuṣe›. Line 1 opens with the last syllable of 10.127.8 and a varga number, then the heading khilāni and the Ratri khila (ā rātri pārthivaṃ rajaḥ), which runs to 116r line 2. The next page with Rigveda text, fol. 116r, begins in RV 10.128.1 ‹mamāgne varco vihaveṣv astu›. Verse 10.127.8 ends on this page; 10.127.8 begins on fol. 114r.
